fidelity.repair_workflow: Standard (and the only one with a deterministic result): never let the model draw the product. (1) PRODUCT LOCK: from the brand's own packshots make clean cutouts per angle, 100%-zoom crops of every label panel, colour references and the approved-claims list. (2) STILLS: generate the world (set, light, props, hands/model if any) with the product reference in place, then in Photoshop mask the generated bottle and COMPOSITE the real cutout over it, relight with Harmonize (Adobe: 'blend an image into a new background in seconds' — BUT 'Your added element will be recreated', i.e. Harmonize itself regenerates the product's pixels, so afterwards re-overlay the untouched packshot layer and carry over only light and shadow via masked/luminosity layers, or relight by hand), paint contact shadow/reflections, mask any fingers that overlap, check every label panel at 100% against the lock. Where the shot is packshot-in-scene, generate the background AROUND the real cutout so the product pixels are never regenerated. (3) FILM: build each 3-5 s shot from two composited keyframes (first/last frame), keep product rotation <=~15 deg or move the CAMERA not the bottle, run 4-6 takes per shot, keep the best, and where any frame drifts overlay a tracked/locked still of the real packshot (or cut to a locked-still shot); supers, logo end-card and claims are added in the editor, never generated. (4) QA gate at 100% zoom on stills and frame-by-frame on film (frames 1, mid, last) before the proof board. The vendor's self-serve path does none of step 2-3: it regenerates.
fidelity.minutes_per_still: ESTIMATE (no primary per-still timing found): packshot-in-scene with supplied cutout 12-30 min (place/perspective 1-3, Harmonize + pick variant 1-3, re-overlay the original label layer because Harmonize recreates the element 2-5, shadows/reflections 3-10, 100% label check 1-2, colour 2-5) plus 2-5 min to select from 4-6 candidates; hand/model-holding-product shots 25-60 min (occlusion masking, fingers, skin/hair QA). Floor for QA alone: Photoroom's annotators used a 30-second minimum review per image per reviewer.
fidelity.minutes_per_film: ESTIMATE: 15-20 s hero film of 4-6 shots = 180-360 min at start (storyboard 20-30; composited keyframes 40-90; 20-36 generations reviewed at 1-2 min each 30-70; locked-still/last-frame fixes on 1-3 shots 30-90; edit, music, supers, colour in CapCut 45-90) and ~120-210 min after ~15 campaigns. Anchors: Kalshi ~20-27 generations per usable clip and ~1-2 h per usable clip for one person WITHOUT a label constraint; practitioners run 2-3 or 4-6 takes per 3-5 s segment.

replacement_cost.derivation: An existing marketing analyst runs the vendor's self-serve path: Higgsfield Marketing Studio one-click templates (15 s film max, 720p at 89,2 credits) + the product-photoshoot agent recipe via a chat assistant + Canva resize: KV + 8 stills 2-4 h, film + 3 cutdowns 1-3 h, exports 1-2 h, internal review ~1 h => 5-10 h (ESTIMATE). Salary: Robert Half Guia Salarial 2026, São Paulo, Analista de marketing digital (P/M firms) p25 R$6.050 / p50 R$9.000 / p75 R$11.000 per month (salary only). Loaded ×1,3 (Simples employer) to ×1,65 (non-Simples: 13º 8,33% + férias+1/3 11,11% + FGTS 8% + INSS patronal 20% + RAT/terceiros) — multiplier DERIVED from statutory rates, not sourced as a single figure — over 168 h => R$47-108/h. 5 h × R$47 + R$263 tool = R$497; 10 h × R$108 + R$263 = R$1.343. Cheaper still: Gemini app NB Pro/NB2 (free quota with visible watermark, or Google AI Plus R$49,99) and Google Ads' built-in NB Pro asset generation.
replacement_cost.what_remains_scarce: The 20-30% the brand cannot get from R$500-1.350: (1) a GUARANTEED label-exact product in every frame — base models pass product-fidelity checks only 27-29% of the time and logo/text distortion hits 20,1% of generations (Photoroom), the vendor's self-serve path regenerates rather than composites, and its own recipe admits it cannot verify small text; a human composite of the real packshot converts a ~29% process into ~100%. (2) A hero FILM that keeps the label locked — the one-click path caps at 15 s/720p and regenerates; practitioners need 4-6 takes per shot plus locked-still composites. (3) Beauty taste that does not read as AI — NIQ: consumers readily identify AI ads and call them 'annoying, boring, confusing'; Ipsos Brazil: 62% prefer human-made ads. (4) Claim-safe design in Portuguese — CONAR's 2026 guide makes 'Anunciantes, Agências e demais partes da cadeia' responsible for AI visuals/simulations that mislead on 'atributos, desempenho', and TikTok ads require an AIGC label on fully AI content but not on background edits; knowing how to build a campaign that avoids both is judgement. (5) Coherence across KV/stills/film/3 ratios and (6) one accountable party on a 7-day clock. HOW SCARCE: (1) and (2) are scarce NOW but not durable — any Photoshop-literate designer can composite, Photoroom already sells a Fidelity Layer (+9 pp), fidelity is trainable (5x CER cut in ProductConsistency) and Higgsfield already composites logos in its brand recipe; (3) is Sol's real asset but only provable by a sample; (4) is moderately scarce; (5)-(6) are ordinary agency value.
replacement_cost.scarcity_evidence: Supply of 'AI production' as a skill is abundant: 99Freelas (national, one marketplace, 25 Sep 2026) returns 233 freelancers mentioning Midjourney, 62 Kling, 23 Nano Banana, 12 Higgsfield; of the 10 Higgsfield profiles listed, most registered 2023-2026 with 0 completed projects, e.g. an 'AI Creator' (joined Jul 2026) selling 'criativos publicitários... com IA (Kling, Seedance, Higgsfield) do briefing à peça'; live AI-video projects on 99Freelas draw 12-31 proposals each. ServImage shows the model alone already clears paying buyers on ~70% of US$139-median product tasks. No count of São Paulo art directors selling LABEL-GUARANTEED beauty campaigns was obtainable (Workana and Fiverr returned 403; Behance/LinkedIn not accessible) — that specific combination (beauty taste + fidelity guarantee + PT claim QA) is UNVERIFIED as scarce and is the only defensible positioning.

treadmill.why: Each release makes GENERATION cheaper and FILM better (better for her: same right to charge, lower cost), but it erodes exactly the two differentiators that are measurable today — label repair and multi-shot film — and it does so through vendor-side 'fidelity layers' and templates rather than through general model quality. Evidence: fidelity did NOT move with the general release cycle (Nano Banana Pro, Nov 2025: 28,2% -> Nano Banana 2, Feb 2026: 29,0% in Photoroom's July 2026 test) but DID move with a specialised layer (+9,2 pp) and with targeted fine-tuning (ProductConsistency ~5x CER cut). Google ships a new image model every ~3-4 months (26 Aug 2025, 20 Nov 2025, 26 Feb 2026, 30 Jun 2026) and pushes each into Google Ads/Slides/Vids for free; OpenAI GPT Image 2 (21 Apr 2026) -> 2.5 (8 Sep 2026); Seedance 2.0 (12 Feb 2026); Kling 3.0 (5 Feb 2026) already markets 'text consistency'; Higgsfield Marketing Studio reached 1.500+ one-click templates by 18 Aug 2026 and its brand recipe already composites logos exactly. 12-18 MONTH VIEW (estimate): a vendor-integrated 'product lock' (reference-conditioned generation + automatic composite of the uploaded packshot) reaches self-serve tools, the fidelity premium falls toward zero and one-click film reaches 20-30 s; what survives is taste, claim-safe direction, coherence and accountability — i.e. the business stays viable only if priced as creative direction against the brand's alternative (a real shoot), not as production. Expect price pressure on a R$5.900 HERO; a plan that needs R$5.900 for production alone becomes the brand intern's afternoon.

backlash.implication: It does not block; it STEERS. No Brazilian rule forbids AI in cosmetic ads and CONAR imposes no disclosure duty (primary), but Brazilian consumers say they prefer human-made ads (62%), AI people are the flashpoint (Dove, Aerie, Guess), fully-AI content needs a TikTok AIGC label while background edits do not, and CONAR puts the agency in the chain of responsibility for AI 'simulações' of performance. For haircare/skincare that points to campaigns built on the REAL packshot with AI-made worlds, textures, light, abstract/ingredient motifs and hands or non-result context — and away from synthetic models showing shiny hair or perfect skin as if it were the product's effect. Conveniently that is also the fastest, most compositable, label-safe production grammar. The plan's FAMILY SKU line 'synthetic-model scenes' should become optional and never depict product results.

biggest_flaw: The plan prices PRODUCTION — which the vendor already sells self-serve for about R$500-1.350 of a brand analyst's time plus a US$49 subscription — while leaving the one layer the vendor structurally does not sell (a guaranteed label-exact product in every frame, beauty-grade taste, claim-safe design) implicit and unguaranteed; and its HERO spec (bottle in motion, synthetic models, 8 stills + film + cutdowns) concentrates effort exactly where base models fail most (27-29% product-fidelity pass; text/logo distortion in 20% of outputs; invented copy on rotating bottles), which is also where each vendor release and 'fidelity layer' is closing the gap fastest. Its 4-6 h target is not reachable for that spec (estimate 14-28 h at start, 9-15 h after 15) — though its own '>8 h' kill line is miscalibrated: hours only break the founder's target above ~31-40 h per HERO; the real hours risk is unpaid spec sampling for outbound.
repair: (1) RE-SPEC the HERO around a 'Product Lock' grammar: every product pixel is the brand's real packshot composited into AI-made worlds; product motion by camera over locked stills or <=15 deg keyframed turns; supers/claims added in the editor; no AI-rendered hair/skin results; synthetic models optional and never showing efficacy — this makes ~6-9 h per HERO plausible after ~15 campaigns, keeps most assets on TikTok's 'insignificant edit' side and out of CONAR 'simulação de desempenho' risk. (2) SELL THE GUARANTEE explicitly (THE ACCEPTANCE FINDING): 'every label letter matches your packshot at 100% zoom or we redo it free' — bounded to rework, backed by the composite method, which the vendor cannot offer. (3) PRICE AGAINST THE BRAND'S REAL ALTERNATIVE (a photo + video shoot with model, studio, retouch) not against AI tools, and target brands with no in-house designer; expect the production premium to fall over 12-18 months and move the value statement to direction + accountability. (4) RE-SET THE KILL LINE to realisation: kill if a HERO takes >25-30 h after campaign 5 or realises <R$166/h. (5) BANK a per-brand lock kit (cutouts, label crops, claims list, failure notes) so the second and third launch for the same brand are faster — the only accumulating asset and the closest thing to origination-once in this model. HONEST FLOOR (estimate, demand unmeasured): 1 HERO/month => ≈R$4.350-4.700 net ≈ US$840-905/month; the target needs ~2,0-2,5 HEROs/month at ~R$5.100 contribution each. CHEAPEST NEXT TEST (R$0-263, no client needed): take 3 public Brazilian haircare/skincare packshots; (a) run the intern path (Gemini NB free quota / Higgsfield Marketing Studio one-click) for 30 min per product and count label/logo errors at 100% zoom; (b) run the Product-Lock path for KV + 3 stills + one 5 s clip with a stopwatch. Bar committed in advance: intern path shows >=1 label/logo error in >=50% of outputs AND Sol's path is label-exact in 100% of outputs in <=5 h per product (=> HERO <=15 h). Then show the side-by-sides to 10 brand marketing leads by Portuguese call: >=4 of 10 say they would pay >=R$4.000 for the Product-Lock version on their next launch. Fail either bar => the fidelity gap is not the product; stop.
